{
  "claim": "recover_json_object skips a fenced JSON object with repeated keys instead of resolving them last-wins, so when a later fenced object has duplicate keys and an earlier fenced object is strict-valid, it returns the earlier object rather than the last fenced object.",
  "expected": "For the reproducer, recover_json_object should return ({\"b\": 2}, (\"b\",)) because the last fenced object is scoreable with repeated keys resolved last-wins.",
  "observed": "It returns ({\"a\": 1}, ()) because the fenced pool sets parsed = None for any fenced candidate that fails strict parsing, skipping the duplicate-key candidate, then returns the earlier strict-valid fenced object.",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"a\": 1}\n```\n```json\n{\"b\": 1, \"b\": 2}\n```",
  "source_basis": "The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text ... A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Replies with multiple fenced JSON objects where the last fenced object has repeated keys and an earlier fenced object is strict-valid.",
  "uncertainty": "None; the top-level fallback masks the issue when the duplicate-key object is the only fenced object, but the documented last-fenced rule is still violated with multiple fences."
}
